A42.notes: Both engines, the issue's full viewport matrix (320x568, 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x800) in BOTH color schemes on the home screen: no horizontal overflow anywhere (document scrollWidth <= viewport), the primary action (Choose screenshot) visible and fully inside the viewport with touch targets >= 44 px; the result screen walks the same matrix by resizing one real-OCR page (one real read per engine, then 320/390/768/1280 resize checks on Copy: visible, >= 44 px, inside the frame). Unit-pinned CSS facts: 100dvh (with the vh fallback line only ever preceding a dvh line), safe-area insets, a 44 px minimum touch target (the primary Copy at 56 px keeps a33's >1.2x proportion), and the standard mobile viewport meta — measured: WebKit logs a console error for the Chromium-only interactive-widget key, so the meta carries no engine-specific keys (A01's no-console-errors gate wins; keyboard-open friendliness is the 100dvh shell sizing, not a meta key). The layout keeps no assumption about owning the window: the shell sizes against the frame's dynamic viewport.

A43.notes: Both engines: the app runs inside a cross-origin iframe (the host test page on a second local origin) — the home screen renders, the pick flow runs INSIDE the frame through the real in-browser OCR to the result screen, and the embedding host page records zero page errors. Where the frame blocks clipboard-write WITHOUT an allow= policy (the issue's exact example), Chromium shows the specific, kind fallback ('Copying is blocked here… select the text below and copy it yourself') with no 'Copied' note — never a silent failure; WebKit's in-frame clipboard behavior is attempted and recorded (the test asserts the no-silent-failure invariant: a visible outcome, copied OR explained). Source-scan (unit): no window.top, window.open or window.opener anywhere in shipped source.

junit:docs/evidence/R2-2/junit/host-vitest.xml::host bridge (R2-2, A44/A45) > reportResult replies to the origin the load came from (allow-listed), never "*"
A44.notes: The contract is pure, unit-tested logic in src/host/messaging.ts: parseHostOrigins (URL-encoded comma-separated http(s) origins; invalid entries dropped, never coerced), hostAllowList (build-time VITE_POSTCLIP_HOST_ORIGINS + ?host= query param, de-duplicated; DEFAULT EMPTY — nothing accepted), validateHostLoadImage (origin gate FIRST — a non-allow-listed sender is ignored before its content is inspected or logged; then exact shape: type, Blob/ArrayBuffer image, bounded requestId; then the MIME allow-list image/png|jpeg|webp; then the 32 MiB size cap), replyTargetFor (allow-listed origin or null — never '*'). The bridge (createHostBridge) installs NOTHING when the allow-list is empty or the app is not embedded (standalone usage is byte-for-byte unaffected), posts postclip:ready to each allow-listed origin on boot, replies only to the origin an accepted load came from, and ignores non-allow-listed senders with no reply and no content logging. Documented in docs/INTEGRATION.md (docs-honesty unit-pinned: the message types, the 32 MiB cap and the MIME allow-list in the doc are the code's).

junit:docs/evidence/R2-2/junit/webkit-e2e.xml::a45_message_from_non_allowlisted_origin_is_ignored
A45.notes: Both engines, TWO local origins: the host test page (e2e/fixtures/host/host.html, served on 4199) embeds the app (4173) in a cross-origin iframe. The allow-listed page (http://localhost:4199 allow-listed via ?host=) receives postclip:ready on boot with the app's origin recorded per message; its postclip:load-image (a real PNG Blob) drives the real in-browser OCR inside the frame and the result text (> 40 chars, real OCR output) comes back as postclip:result — every reply's origin asserted to be exactly the app's. The stranger page (http://127.0.0.1:4199, NOT allow-listed while localhost:4199 is) gets NOTHING: its load-image is ignored (no reading state inside the frame within the wait window, home screen intact, zero messages received — an untrusted origin is never replied to, and not even postclip:ready reaches it because the reply targetOrigin never matches). Privacy on both sides: the host page's URL unchanged and its localStorage/sessionStorage empty; the embedded app's localStorage/sessionStorage empty (the only thing that leaves the app is the result postMessage to the allow-listed origin; the demo host keeps the text in the DOM only — that is the feature).

A46.notes: docs/INTEGRATION.md is the single source of truth for hosting and the hand-off: the exact frame-ancestors HTTP header the host must send (a <meta> CSP cannot set frame-ancestors — the spec ignores it in meta policies) with working example configs for the static dist/ this repo builds (nginx, Caddy, and a plain Node static server), the iframe allow=/sandbox recommendation that keeps the app working (allow="clipboard-write" recommended; a sandbox="allow-scripts" variant documented with its honest costs: opaque origin → no service worker, no model cache, clipboard blocked → the kind fallback), and the storage-partitioning reality inside frames (third-party storage is partitioned and often wiped; the app works with ephemeral storage — the rules cleanup needs none, and the model cache case links to A39's first-class volatile handling). The docs-honesty unit suite pins the doc to the code (message types, 32 MiB cap, MIME allow-list, the never-"*" reply rule, the default-empty allow-list). The A15 no-storage audit re-ran green on this tree (this slice's junit) — the contract adds exactly one allowed channel (the result postMessage to the allow-listed origin) and no post text enters any URL, storage, console or network request on either side (asserted per-flow in the a45 spec too).

limitations: Real WebView embedding (Android System WebView, iOS WKWebView) is NOT_RUN on this runner (A27): the e2e coverage uses Playwright's Chromium and WebKit with a real cross-origin iframe from a second local server — the same embedding mechanics a WebView uses, but not the real shells.

WebKit's clipboard-write behavior inside a cross-origin iframe without allow= is not deterministically blockable on this matrix; the a43 test asserts the engine-invariant (a visible outcome, copied OR explained) and Chromium (deterministically blocked) pins the specific kind fallback message. Attempted and recorded, never faked.

The origin allow-list travels in the ?host= query parameter (URL-encoded origins only, never post content); a host that cannot control its embed URL should use the build-time VITE_POSTCLIP_HOST_ORIGINS instead. Both are documented in docs/INTEGRATION.md.
The host channel bounds images at 32 MiB and the MIME allow-list to png/jpeg/webp (the formats the sniff stage reads); a host needing other formats would be a plan change, not a config.

postclip:result may arrive more than once for a requestId when the optional (off-by-default) model cleanup upgrades the text after the standard result — the last one wins; documented in docs/INTEGRATION.md.
Real-device behavior (real mobile share sheets, real WebViews, real OS clipboards) stays NOT_RUN (A27/A30, the plan's optional device pass).
